body:
DECIDED BY MYK, 2026-08-17, in chat: D1 takes the GRANT-VERB option. A connection gets authority to
register through an ordinary grant carrying a new `register` verb, SCOPED TO AN ENTITY-NAMESPACE
PREFIX. Root registration stays the operator's. No container acquires a signing identity.

  loam grant --verb=register --prefix="thread:" <connector>
  # the connector may then register thread:* and nothing else

WHAT THAT DECISION COLLAPSES, and this is why the ticket is now small:
- D2 is MOOT. No container operator means no question of where a connection's container comes from.
  The board cards for T118 and T119 are no longer prerequisites, and this ticket does not wait on them.
- D3 is ANSWERED by construction: a registration binds within the prefix its grant names, nowhere else.
- R3 (entity-namespace collisions between scopes) is ANSWERED by construction: the prefix IS the
  partition. Two connectors holding `thread:` and `note:` cannot collide.
- The §28 reading that would have made this "not new design" is retired. §28 says trust is a property
  of a CONTAINER; it does not say a container carries its own KEY, and the code reads
  `gw.operatorAuthor` everywhere. That gap stays unbuilt and unclaimed.

WHY THIS SHAPE IS RIGHT rather than merely smaller: grants already carry a verb, read AT THE VERB by
the door — `write` and `admin` exist today in accounts.ts, and `loam pen create` reads standing at the
verb precisely so an admin grant is not write standing. Registration becomes one more verb in a
vocabulary that already governs authority, with revocation that already binds at once. Nothing new is
invented; an existing primitive is extended.

STILL TRUE, from the measurement that opened this ticket (a session on 2026-08-17 drove the live
connector with a non-operator token):
1. `loam_register` ships on the MCP door; the refusal is about authority, not capability.
2. The refusal reads `registration is constitutional: it requires an operator token`.
3. IT FIRES BEFORE SHAPE VALIDATION, and that ordering is load-bearing: a malformed probe still drew
   the authority refusal, so a non-operator cannot fingerprint the registration format by diffing
   error messages. PRESERVE IT under the new tier.
4. Claims work; a mutation landed one signed delta and returned the re-resolved view.
5. Membership is separate from evidence: an entity can hold a claim and be on no board.
6. Retraction is not erasure — fields fall to null, the `_hex` moves, the deltas remain.
7. The write landed in the ROOT namespace because there was nowhere else to put it. That is what the
   prefix now answers.

THE BUILD:
- A `register` verb in the grant vocabulary, carrying a prefix. Decide how the prefix rides the grant;
  a pointer role beside subject and verb is the shape that matches accounts.ts today.
- The registration door reads standing AT THE VERB and checks the proposed entity against the granted
  prefix. The operator keeps root.
- `loam grant list` shows the verb and the prefix, so an operator can read what they handed out.
- `loam grant revoke` already binds at once; assert that here rather than assuming it.

RAILS, red first:
1. A connector holding `register` at prefix `thread:` registers `thread:groove`; the type appears and
   serves at that surface.
2. The same token registering `note:anything` is REFUSED — the prefix is a fence, not a hint.
3. The same token registering at root is refused with the EXISTING message, byte for byte, so a client
   learns nothing new about whether root registration is possible for anyone (§12/T78).
4. ORDERING HOLDS UNDER BOTH TIERS: a malformed payload from an authorized caller refuses on SHAPE; a
   malformed payload from an unauthorized caller refuses on AUTHORITY.
5. Re-registration at the same entity within the prefix EVOLVES the type — iterating a schema is the
   whole point of the feature — and a re-registration that would drop `writable` refuses loudly and
   names the field. That is T96's failure traffic; the fix is landed and this is its exercise.
6. `loam grant revoke` kills the register standing at once, and the next registration refuses.
7. Two-sided: a bystander connector holding a different prefix is unaffected by either the grant or
   the revocation.

STILL OPEN, carried forward unchanged:
R2 — a schema is DATA; a renderer bundle is CODE. This ticket registers schemas only. Renderer
submission is its own ticket and inherits §24.5's quarantine bill rather than inventing a budget.
R4 — ejection and erasure: a scope that can be ejected carries its registrations out, and once a schema
has left it cannot be erased. Any erasure report must name ejected scopes as unreachable.
R5 — the listing door materializes a curated container per hyperschema. Scoped registrations multiply
hyperschemas; check that T163's index and refresh path do not fan out per scope.

TIER: Myk's merge — it adds an authority verb, which changes what the system promises. The DESIGN
question is settled, so this is buildable rather than design-stage.


OVERTAKEN (stale sweep, 2026-08-25): PR #429 landed the whole build: accounts.ts:49 adds "register" to the Verb set with the prefix fence (`fenceAdmits`, line 89) and the fourth `prefix` pointer (lines 112-133), cli.ts:2213+ ships `loam grant --verb=register --prefix`, and all three declared rails exist (test/gateway/register-fence.test.ts, test/server/register-verb.test.ts, test/cli/grant-register.test.ts); review follow-ups were minted as their own tickets in #430. The shard still reads in_progress — it is an archive candidate, not open work.
title: An authorized connection registers inside its own namespace — a grantable register verb
